title: Competitive displacement in the grass-bushes-trees process on a scale-free network
summary: The grass-bushes-trees process is a two-type contact process in which the types face asymmetric birth mechanisms. Vertices of a graph can either be occupied by a tree, occupied by a bush, or empty (containing grass). The trees die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $λ_{\mathcal T}$ on any neighbouring vertex (possibly taking the place of a bush). Bushes die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $λ_{\mathcal B}$ on any empty neighbouring vertex; in particular, they are forbidden from taking the place of trees.
